issues.claim: "the building is staffed 8am–7pm on weekdays" (intro), repeated in the founder email and the walk-in opener
issues.problem: Contradicted by the practice's own hours page, which lists Mon–Thu 8:00am–7:00pm but Friday 8:00am–5:00pm (Saturday 8–5, Sunday 8–2). Friday is a weekday, so 8–7 is wrong for at least one weekday. The same site's employment page also states technicians staff the hospital "from 8 am until at least 7 pm, seven days a week, including holidays", which the audit ignores — so the framing overstates the weekday gap and understates weekend presence.
issues.fix: Replace with the posted hours verbatim ("Mon–Thu 8–7, Fri/Sat 8–5, Sun 8–2, with technicians on site until at least 7pm seven days a week per the employment page") in the intro, the email and the opener, and keep the point as the contrast between 24-hour emergency advertising and posted client-facing hours rather than a staffing gap.

issues.problem: The body (title through the closing disclaimer, excluding the 'For the founder' section and the Sources list) is roughly 500–515 words, about 12% over the ~450-word target.
issues.fix: Cut ~60 words: drop the third 'Why this works' bullet or fold it into the second, tighten the three 'Now:' paragraphs to one sentence each, and shorten section headings.

issues.claim: "Businesses like yours often find the same protocol questions get re-asked every few months" (§3, Now)
issues.problem: Unsourced generalisation about other businesses, presented as fact with no citation and no 'inference' framing.
issues.fix: Ground it in the practice's own page instead: the employment application asks whether an applicant can "learn the various protocols and adjust accordingly (after one or two weeks)" because "each doctor may do similar procedures differently" — cite https://sayrebrookvet.com/employment-application/ and label the rest as an inference.

issues.claim: "With about a dozen people covering clinic, boarding and housecalls" (intro)
issues.problem: The only support cited is the LinkedIn company page, which returned HTTP 403 on re-check, so the headcount could not be independently confirmed. The 11–50 band alone does not establish ~12.
issues.fix: Attribute it ("LinkedIn lists 12 employees at the practice") or soften to "a small team of roughly a dozen, per its LinkedIn listing"; do not state a headcount without a source the reader can open.

issues.claim: "staff profiles show people moving from boarding to pharmacy to lab" (§3, Now)
issues.problem: Partly accurate but overstated. The employee-of-the-month page shows one technician moving from boarding technician to pharmacy/outpatient technician, and a second person working as animal caretaker, veterinary assistant and laboratory technician. It does not show a boarding → pharmacy → lab progression.
issues.fix: Rephrase to "staff profiles show one technician who moved from boarding to pharmacy and another covering caretaking, assisting and lab work" — https://sayrebrookvet.com/employee-of-the-month/.

issues.claim: "Urgent calls, routine calls and callbacks all land on the same small team, seven days a week" (§1, Now)
issues.problem: An inference from a single published phone number and a small staff, stated as established fact with no source that says calls are answered by that team.
issues.fix: Add a hedge such as "as far as the public pages show, urgent calls, routine calls and callbacks all route to the same main number" and keep the conclusion in the inference framing used in analysis.json.

issues.claim: Email draft: "I left a short note at your front desk about your emergency line"
issues.problem: Asserts a completed action that the folder's own plan only sequences (walk-in note, then email within 48 hours); nothing confirms the note has been delivered, so sending this as written risks a false statement to the recipient. It also calls the main number "your emergency line" when the site routes after-hours emergencies to the general line.
issues.fix: Send only after the note is actually dropped off, or change to "I dropped off a short note at your front desk earlier today" once true, and say "your after-hours emergency number (the main line)".
